brief:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Wednesday he opposed launching a preemptive attack on Iran before the country's October 27 election, Al-Monitor reported. The statement came as Netanyahu cautioned Tehran and its proxies against striking Israel.

The remarks signal Netanyahu's reluctance to initiate major military action in the immediate run-up to voting, though they do not preclude operations after the election takes place.
dek: JERUSALEM, Oct 14 (Reuters) - Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Wednesday that he was not in favour of a preemptive strike against Iran before Israel's October 27 election but also warned Tehran and its proxies against striking Israel.
title: Netanyahu rules out Iran strike before Israel election
